rating_cap: The RF-EQ-001 + RF-OBS-001 + RF-DISC-002 cross-module forensic mosaic is a compound High flag and caps any long at Starter Position Only, with no edge bypass. No Critical governance, solvency, fraud, or going-concern lock fired. The no-proven-edge ceiling is 60 and valuation confidence is separately capped at 55 by the 51.14% method spread. Watchlist is stricter than each positive-rating ceiling.
variant_perception_summary: Visa's network quality and double-digit activity growth are widely visible. The possible edge is that the market may underweight the recent quality gap: incentives grew faster than net revenue, reported margin fell, and cash from operations declined while revenue rose. That hypothesis is not proven because the cash divergence is unexplained and the four-quarter beat record is favorable; therefore there is no proven variant perception yet.
what_everyone_knows: Visa has a strong global payment network, June-2026 LTM revenue grew 14.4%, Q3 payment volume and processed transactions each grew 10%, and revenue plus vendor-defined normalized EPS beat consensus in each of the last four quarters. The four-quarter sample is judgmental evidence, not an empirical base rate.
what_is_priced_in: At the $364.15 pool anchor, a 9.04% WACC requires roughly 19.67% annual free-cash-flow growth for five years. A lower 7.15% implied WACC reconciles the modeled base cash path to price, so the reverse-DCF is a demanding conditional hurdle rather than proof the market is wrong.
what_market_may_be_missing: Q3 client incentives grew 18% versus 14% net-revenue growth, GAAP-derived EBITDA margin fell 157 basis points to 62.3%, and LTM CFO fell 3.9% while revenue rose 14.4%. The cause of the cash divergence is not proven from available data, so this is an earnings-quality hypothesis rather than a misconduct claim.
edge_proof: The no-position thesis is weakened if Visa reports FQ4 FY2026 revenue of at least $12.339bn, GAAP-derived EBITDA margin of at least the matched 60.3% prior-year quarter, and better full-year CFO/EBITDA conversion. It is strengthened by revenue at or below $11.855bn, margin below 60.3%, or further cash-conversion deterioration.
killer_risk: Visa earns the bull-case $36.720bn of NTM vendor EBITDA and the market pays 22.34x, producing $425.88 per share and making the no-position call too cautious.

error_defense_evidence.bad base rate: The FQ4 revenue bar is matched to audited FQ4 FY2025 revenue, and the four-quarter beat history is labelled judgment rather than an empirical frequency [analyses/V_2026-09-23/earnings/05_beat-miss-setup.md, §§1 and 6].
error_defense_evidence.valuation multiple error: The thesis carries the 51.14% independent-method dispersion, does not assume sector-cycle stability, and uses own-history and peer multiples as conditional anchors rather than independent proof of mispricing [analyses/V_2026-09-23/valuation/07_scenario-and-fair-value.md, §§1–5].
error_defense_evidence.bad causal inference: Only the filed 1 percentage-point FX contribution is treated as directly explained; the remaining 13.4 percentage points, about 93% of Q3 revenue growth, remain an explicit residual [analyses/V_2026-09-23/earnings/02_revenue-drivers.md, §6a; analyses/V_2026-09-23/earnings/99_earnings-synthesis.md, §§2–3].
error_defense_evidence.false negative: The scenario set retains the valuation module's $425.88 bull case, a 16.95% upside state, rather than narrowing the distribution around the negative base case [analyses/V_2026-09-23/valuation/07_scenario-and-fair-value.md, §3; analyses/V_2026-09-23/final_thesis.md, §8].
error_defense_evidence.timing error: The expected 2026-10-27 FQ4/FY2026 date is repeatedly labelled Capital IQ-derived and not issuer-confirmed; proven debt-maturity months are kept separate [analyses/V_2026-09-23/catalyst/99_catalyst-synthesis.md, §§1–2].
